-i: The target computer to connect to
-u: The username to log in with
-p: The password to log in with — this shows up as plain text, so watch out for it leaking into logs or shell history
-s: A folder of scripts on your machine that get uploaded and can be run on the target — this is real code execution on the target
-e: A folder of programs on your machine, ready to be sent and run on the target — high risk, same as delivering a payload onto the machine
-S: Connects using an encrypted (SSL) connection, usually on port 5986
-P: Which port to connect to (5985 normally, 5986 for SSL)
-l: Saves a log of everything done in the session
--no-colors: Turns off colored text in the output
